A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Flow4R work. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original Flow4R tracking and reconstruction results, motion-representation ablations, and qualitative predictions in Section 4.

after.justification: V2 retains the original tracking, reconstruction, and ablation results and adds throughput and GPU-memory measurements in Section 4.4.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same shared two-view architecture, direct outputs {P, Pvt, W, C}, weighted pose solver, five training losses and weights, and anchored-pair scale alignment. Rewritten explanations do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Training datasets and evaluation coverage remain unchanged: WorldTrack tracking on ADT, Dynamic Replica, Point Odyssey, and Panoptic Studio, plus reconstruction on Point Odyssey and TUM-Dynamics. Removing one Point Odyssey visualization does not remove that dataset or its task coverage.

E2.justification: The qualitative tracking comparison drops POMATO: v1 Figure 4 compares POMATO, St4RTrack, and Flow4R, whereas v2 Figure 5 retains only St4RTrack and Flow4R. Quantitative comparator membership in Tables 1–3 is unchanged; the new efficiency comparison uses St4RTrack.

E3.justification: V2 adds an efficiency evaluation on an RTX PRO 6000 GPU using throughput in pairs/s and VRAM in MB. Existing training budgets, WorldTrack alignment, APD thresholds, and first-64-frame evaluation remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 adds an analysis of throughput versus memory consumption. The three-way motion-representation ablation is unchanged. Qualitative analysis is slightly reduced by omitting POMATO's comparison panels and the Point Odyssey 3D example from v1 Figure 5.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the empirical comparisons. V2's efficiency table does not introduce statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V2 Table 4 newly reports Flow4R at 26.8 pairs/s and 3152 MB versus St4RTrack at 27.9 pairs/s and 6711 MB. All numerical results in Tables 1–3 remain unchanged. Some qualitative result panels are removed, without changing the retained findings.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, geometric relations, losses, and appendix notation remain equivalent. V1's two numbered total-loss lines become one equation in v2. No new proof, formal assumption, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: Both versions claim unified reconstruction and tracking through scene flow, a shared two-view model without explicit pose heads or bundle adjustment, and competitive or state-of-the-art performance. Replacing much of the 'minimal' terminology with 'compact' and emphasizing existing sequence processing do not materially change contribution scope.

C2.justification: V2 Section 4.2 adds an explicit explanation that both F and Pvt are invariant to the choice of reference objects, distinguishing them from Pv and Pt. The limitations concerning scarce flow annotations, two-view inputs, and constrained online tracking are retained rather than newly introduced.

D1.justification: V2 specifies RTX PRO 6000 hardware for the new efficiency measurements. Existing training hardware, schedules, data-processing sources, and project access information remain unchanged. Appendix hyperparameters already present in v1 Table 4 are retained in v2 Table 6.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds C4D and describes its combination of feedforward reconstruction, optimized correspondence matching, and a learned mobility mask. The broader research positioning is retained; reference renumbering and publication metadata updates do not constitute additional new works.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, related work, method explanations, and conclusion while largely preserving scientific meaning. It shifts terminology toward 'compact,' separates training data from training details and benchmarks from metrics, labels limitations explicitly, and adds appendix introductory prose.

P2.justification: The entire document changes from a two-column to a single-column layout, with widespread figure and table relocation and resizing. V2 rearranges and trims the qualitative comparison, reduces the 3D visualization to two examples, adds the efficiency table, and redistributes the appendix tables across separate pages.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful measured efficiency evidence in Section 4.4 and clarifies the reasoning behind its motion representation while preserving the main accuracy results and reproducibility details. Removing POMATO's qualitative panels and one Point Odyssey example slightly reduces illustrative breadth, and the profiling protocol remains brief. The net gain is useful but limited, without a substantial change to the method or its validation.
